vmware-solution-reservation-steady.title: Compare a reservation for steadily running hosts
vmware-solution-reservation-steady.body: These Azure VMware Solution hosts are priced pay as you go and are expected to run for a year or longer. Microsoft says committing to a reserved instance saves money; reservations are sold for AV36P, AV48, AV52 and AV64 hosts (1 year, and 3 years for AV48 and AV64). Compare the reservation price, keeping in mind the Enterprise Agreement or Microsoft Customer Agreement requirement.

citation.source: Save costs with Azure VMware Solution reserved instances
citation.quote: you save money. The reservation discount automatically applies to the running Azure VMware Solution hosts that match the reservation scope and attributes.

vmware-solution-reservation-eligibility.title: Reservations need an Enterprise Agreement or Microsoft Customer Agreement
vmware-solution-reservation-eligibility.body: This estimate uses an Azure VMware Solution reservation. Microsoft lists eligibility conditions for buying it: the customer needs an Azure Enterprise Agreement or a Microsoft Customer Agreement. Confirm the customer has one before relying on this price.

citation.source: Save costs with Azure VMware Solution reserved instances
citation.quote: You need an Azure Enterprise Agreement (EA) or a Microsoft Customer Agreement (MCA) with Microsoft.

vmware-solution-av64-prerequisite.title: AV64 hosts need an existing cluster of another host type
vmware-solution-av64-prerequisite.body: This option has AV64 hosts and no other Azure VMware Solution host type. Microsoft says an AV64 Gen 1 host can only be added to a private cloud that already has at least 3 hosts of AV36P, AV48 or AV52, so the estimate is likely missing those base hosts. Add them, or confirm the region offers AV64 Gen 2 or that the customer already has the base cluster.

citation.quote: An Azure VMware Solution private cloud deployed with at least 3 nodes of AV36P, AV48 or AV52 is required prior to adding AV64.
